title: WPSS/1893/2018 of Bhagat Singh Vs Union Of India AND OTHERS

paras.text:
WPSS No. 1893 of 2018
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Mr. Harendra Belwal, Advocate for
the petitioner.
Mrs. Monika Pant, Standing Counsel
for Union of India.
By means of present writ petition,
petitioner has sought the following reliefs:-
(i) Issue a writ order or direction in the
nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to grant the
benefit of the 1st and 2nd ACP forthwith
under financial up-gradation scheme to the
petitioner.
(ii) Issue a writ rule order or direction in
the nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to provide benefit
of 6th Pay Commission to the petitioner
from the date it becomes due.
(iii) Issue a writ rule order or direction in
the nature of mandamus commanding and
directing the respondents to give arrears of
the 1st and 2nd ACP forthwith under
financial up-gradation scheme to the
petitioner with compounding interest as
well as arrears accrued to the petitioner
under benefits of 6th Pay Commission with
compounding interest immediately.
Learned Standing Counsel appearing
for Union of India would submit that relief,
claimed by the petitioner, is not
maintainable as petitioner has to approach
the Central Administrative Tribunal for
redressal of his grievance.
On the other hand, learned counsel
for the petitioner would submit that
petitioner is an old aged and sick person
and is unable to litigate with Union of
India. He confined his prayer only to the
extent that petitioner be permitted to move
representation before the authority
concerned for redressal of his grievance
and direction may be issued to the
authority concerned to take decision on

the representation of the petitioner within
some specific time frame.
 The prayer made by learned counsel
for the petitioner is innocuous and worth
accepting.
 Accordingly, the writ petition is
disposed of directing the petitioner to
make fresh representation before the
authority concerned/respondents, who in
turn shall decide the representation, so
moved by the petitioner, as per Rules, by
passing a speaking and reasoned order
within a period of six weeks from today
from the date of production of certified
copy the order.
Pending application, if any, also
stands disposed of.
(Lok Pal Singh, J.)
Parul 17.09.2019
